questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Scottish nature and culture. The possibility for outdoor experiences. Erasmus grant. Architecture and history of the city. Language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. The university website is informative and the mails from Visiting Student Office were plentiful as well. Maybe, sometimes they gave a bit of an overload of information and it could be difficult to dissect which information was actually essential.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was given a Student Advisor, who sent me mails and whom I could always contact. It would have been nice if the assistance provided was more in person rather than just over mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively difficult to find housing and everything was very expensive. I would recommend to look for housing with other exchange students and to use the app SpareRoom.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to have your own place. As of what I've heard, uni accommodations are as expensive as off campus housing, and you have to buy all your own utensils and stuff if you live in uni accommodation, thus, I thought it was much nicer to have a fully furnished apartment off campus. Moreover, if you want uni accommodation, you have to contact them regularly and be very insisting even if you have signed up for it, which is frustrating.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very bureaucratic, confusing and long.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always contact your Student Advisor for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was relatively successful. I didn't get my first two priorities, but I still got courses that I was very interested in attending.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: During Welcome Week, a lot of students are arriving and the queues are long, but you still have time the following weeks so don't stress. And always ask for help if you're in doubt. Everything usually works out just fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had a first year, a second year and a third year course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was structured with two lectures of the duration of an hour and one tutorial each week. The room and culture around studying isn't very social. Social life isn't centered around teaching but extracurricular activities (societies and clubs).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Social Anthropology, Contemporary Cinema and Science, Sorcery and Wonder in Islam.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Science, Sorcery and Wonder in Islam, because the lecturer was very passionate, it was an interesting and niche course. Moreover, the course was not too big so you could manage to get a friend or two in class as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Prices for membership of clubs and societies.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent is very expensive, transportation can be expensive but if you buy a Ridacard, it's manageable. Grocery shopping was cheap but dining out was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Anything that your heart can desire.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Mountaineering Club or the Hillwalking Club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out of town, rent a car, borrow a tent for wild camping (it's free), hike.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Scottish people in the service industry are extremely kind and chatty.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Explore the pub culture and live music/jamming scene, go at least once to an evening with Ceilidh dance at Stramash and sign up for one society or club and attend as many events as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Exploring the Scottish Highlands.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Always being proactive for experiencing new stuff, making most of the city and socializing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
